summary: Working across a range of clients, creating both admin and public facing interfaces.
Projects to date have been developed either in React (with Typescript and Jest testing), or custom Shopify templates.

Having recently delivered a React built front end for an AI prototype project, then taken a side quest helping out on a mobile app, I am back with a chunky React project integrating with a .NET backend.

projects.title: Head Office wages and reporting system
projects.thumbAlt: news icon
description: A back-office platform for a multi-site salon chain, built around a Head Office System that allows users with different permission levels, such as senior management, payroll or area managers, to review, edit and submit staff wage sheets across their assigned locations. The application talks to a .Net API which coordinates with the EPOS system the salons run in-house.

A bespoke feature enjoyed is a salon performance map on the leadership dashboard. I created a custom dot-style illustration of the UK, then wrote a coordinate projection method that converts real latitude and longitude values into pixel positions on the graphic - effectively calibrating the image to a geographic bounding box. The result is an interactive SVG component that plots each salon as a pin, highlights top performers, and responds to hover state with an animated marker, all without reaching for a mapping library.

The project is being developed on a tight schedule, and I've been deliberate about leveraging Claude AI to keep momentum up. Strong upfront context setting - architecture documents, conventions, and a living project status file — means the AI can contribute meaningfully to implementation while I focus on review, verification, and the decisions that require real judgement. It's given me a sharper sense of where AI genuinely accelerates a build and where careful human oversight remains essential.

projects.title: Inizio Ignite
projects.thumbAlt: news icon
description: Whilst the project details are under NDA wraps, I am allowed to say that I am working on a mobile app for the healthcare sector.
So I'm starting the year learning Dart and Flutter.
In my ancient history I made iOS press release apps for Jaguar Land Rover and Bentley - fast performance, very heavy on imagery and video. Developed using ActionScript, amazingly.
This will have shades of the familiar, but mostly be completely different. An exciting journey!

projects.title: "Polaris View" - AI underwriting tool
projects.thumbAlt: Polaris logo
description: Front end developer in a crack squad, building the interface for a human-in-the-loop AI project.

This started as a rapid development prototype, required to meet a tight demonstration deadline but has moved into a client-facing product. For the prototype, I roughed out a functioning interface with vanilla JSX, then leveraged Claude to refine the build, including proper TypeScript interfaces, and accessibility features.
This met the original speed requirements, and also created a more solid base for further development with little additional overhead.
This approach also gave me space to consider the position and value of AI in my workflow, getting a clearer understanding of the values it can bring.
The codebase is now in production with a pre-existing dedicated client team, so I've handed over development responsibilities while continuing to support and guide the team as required.
projects.techStack: React (Vite), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules, Claude

projects.title: Multiple Shopify stores
projects.thumbAlt: Wolfson Brands logo
description: Wolfson Brands run multiple Shopify stores, with European and global markets. I have been working across their range, introducing new features and maintaining existing ones.

I developed my role in the squad to include elements of team support both for the squad manager and team colleagues, covering elements of backlog refinement and sprint planning, general team support and code reviews, in addition to my front end development.
projects.techStack: JS, Shopify Liquid, CSS, Tailwind CSS

projects.title: Neon effect SVG. Internal branding
projects.thumbAlt: ClearSky branding
description: Following a chat with the marketing team, I grabbed a quiet moment to create a small series of internal branding animations based on the neon identity ClearSky have around the office.

Following up on the intrigue created by the animation, in a second quiet moment I repurposed the code to create a Neon drawing tool as part of a demonstration of the flexibility and power of SVGs for an internal Brown Bag Lunch session.

projects.title: Zonal admin SaaS
projects.thumbAlt: Zonal logo
description: Zonal are the market leaders in point of sale services for the hospitality industry.

They have an established client side offering, but were in the process of moving their services to the cloud. CSL stepped in to help crunch on some back- and front-end processes in their admin interface.

summary: Working primarily on government and public sector websites, with a focus on clear UX and accessibility.
Projects generally involved JSX prototyping within a Preact framework and subsequently working with the .Net or Umbraco teams to realise the final build.

Sometimes rapid prototyping was required, for example exploring charting libraries, the OpenSystemsLab geo-data mapping API, or creating bespoke JS/SVG tools. Where these moved into production, I managed the integration, produced documentation and provided training as required.

projects.title: AI Dynamic Forms
projects.thumbAlt: Colourful flow chart diagram with dummy data
description: Building on a long-term understanding of Scot.Gov requirements, Storm undertook a project to use AI to auto-generate forms from a variety of sources.

As the lead front end developer my primary role was to ensure a coherent front end design, and provide any DOM manipulation JavaScript. In addition, throughout the project daily stand-ups provided the space for me to reflect on the UI, UX and accessibility directions the (backend driven) build was taking, and keeping it honest!

A small UX discussion about visual representations of a user's journey through a complex chart led to me implementing the Mermaid charting library which swiftly became a central pillar of the project's UI.
projects.techStack: JS, Mermaid, CSS, .Net Razor template integration

projects.title: Smart Apps - Planning and Payments
projects.thumbAlt: Map with highlighted building boundary
description: A large scale Scot.Gov project to review the existing online planning permission process.

As the lead front end developer on the project I implemented the Scot.Gov design system, integrated with Storm's own design agnostic scaffold. I was responsible for ensuring that during the process of .Net implementation WCAG 2.2 accessibility standards were maintained, and providing any DOM manipulation or forms related JavaScript as required.

One such custom element was a tool for accurately mapping the boundaries of a property. For this we used the OpenSystemsLab geo-data mapping API, and you can see a test implementation via the link below.
The project is not yet live, but the Scot.Gov Digital Planning team intends to take the alpha service prototypes forward to beta and live, in line with its digital strategy.
projects.techStack: JSX, JS, CSS, .Net Razor template integration

projects.title: Glasgow Club website
projects.thumbAlt: Glasgow Club logo
description: Following the Glasgow Life transformation, Storm was tasked with a similar overhaul of the sister site, Glasgow Club.

Glasgow Club has a distinct design language from other sites in the group, so whilst the underlying scaffold is largely shared across the estate, as lead front end developer on the project, I needed to take care that all details of their design were implemented correctly.

Whilst many of the challenges from Glasgow Life had been solved for this build, the scale of tabular data presented for venues and activities proved an issue. Smaller tables (opening times) maintained visual structure and only changed width responsively. Larger tables required a visual collapsing of <td> elements, whilst maintaining DOM structure and coherence for keyboard users.

projects.title: Glasgow Life website
projects.thumbAlt: Glasgow Life logo
description: Storm took Glasgow Life through a complete digital transformation programme, redeveloping their main web portal, and dedicated venue and event sites.
As the lead front end developer on the project I ensured the design was faithfully implemented, and ensured accessibility standards were maintained.

Interesting challenges included the map view for the venue finder, bespoke Swiper carousel conflicts, and much longer than expected horizontal in-page navigations. However, working closely with the design, UX, and testing teams, all issues were resolved to the client's satisfaction.

projects.title: Full estate cookie banner update
projects.thumbAlt: Historic Environment Scotland webpage, showing cookie consent banner
description: The Historic Environment Scotland (HES) estate comprises some 30+ separately maintained websites, built over many years with multiple technologies. And they all needed to have their cookie banner updated and WCAG 2.2 compliant.

My role was to adapt their existing cookie banner code for compliance (specifically ensuring no interactive elements are obscured), to be standardised for all sites, with configuration options, but without the need for an implementing developer to customise the JavaScript.

Final delivery was with a .umd JavaScript bundle with a configuration object in a <script> tag. I provided extensive documentation for HES developers to use, and was available for support when some implementations were less straightforward and the HES developer needed assistance.

projects.title: Desktop booking app
projects.thumbAlt: Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal logo and a schematic of a few desks
description: When the COPFS started to return to office work after lockdown, they needed a tool to allow staff to book desk space. I converted paper office layout charts into data, in JSON format, which allowed all offices and desks to be dynamically drawn and interacted with. Booking data was submitted to their existing SharePoint intranet.

links.label: As the full application is an intranet, there is no public URL.

summary: I first approached Realise as a Flash/ActionScript developer looking to transition into HTML5 work. I had a little JS / CSS / HTML experience, and although I had 14 years Flash experience I was wet behind my HTML5 ears.
However, Realise had a few banner clients which needed to be transitioned to HTML5 builds, and I had made a lot of banners at Wunderman and Saint (RKCR/Y&R), and the deal was struck.
I made a build pipeline in Gulp, set guides and processes, and arranged training so other team members could join the fun.

Banners production sat in Support, so I also worked on (amongst others) Standard Life Investments and Lloyds Banking Group CMS sites, using Teamsite and Ektron. In addition, I helped in development teams for multiple smaller projects, and championed team learning through skill share exercises and addressed topics like Imposter Syndrome and general mental health.

projects.title: British and Irish Lions: Game
projects.thumbAlt: Game image of drone exploding as it is hit with a rugby ball
description: Drone Kick game.
Part of the "One Team. One Standard." British and Irish Lions tour sponsorship campaign.

Written with vanilla JavaScript, this is a simple target shoot game. Gameplay needed to be the same on mobile and desktop so the interaction is necessarily simple: automatic missile direction control and one click to fire.
The game can work in a standalone configuration for conferences, with a leaderboard mode to display the top ten scores on a separate screen.
Over 64,500 plays in a month, with an average 44 plays per person.
The campaign (game and banners) was awarded BT Sport Industry Award: Best Ambassador, Influencer or Partnership of the Year.

It was a quick and enjoyable project which is still alive on the client site 5 years later. Now that's something to sing about!

projects.title: Interactive folding Brompton
projects.thumbAlt: Graphic of folding Brompton bike
description: I am a huge Brompton bike fanboy, so when I heard AmazeRealise was pitching to them I had to butt in, and quickly knocked up this responsively animated, interactive Brompton bike banner.
Moving through the three main steps in the bike's amazing fold, the user can also customise the paint, just like ordering the real thing (used to be).
Born out of personal passion, whilst the pitch wasn't successful, this illustrates how all parts of a team can pull together and produce something unexpected.

training.intro: Learning is a life-long thing. In addition to extended Josh Comeau courses, recently I've been snacking short courses at Frontend Masters to refresh and extend 25+ years of experience.

courses.title: Engineering Management 101 & 102
courses.description: I actively enjoy my development work, but within squads I find myself taking on mentoring and somewhat-management roles. I took these courses to gain greater understanding of this area, and to build some foundational skills. The second course delved deeper into the principles of effective engineering management and probably took me past where I project myself being for now. However, it was really useful in helping me understand the breadth of management tasks, and will certainly be useful for my skills as a senior team member.

courses.title: TypeScript Fundamentals 5+ / TypeScript: From First Steps to Professional
courses.description: Whilst I had brushed up against TypeScript, I never really needed to apply it until I joined ClearSky. I wanted more than a passing understanding based on code picking, so I enrolled in these courses to underpin and grow my understanding.

links.label: First Steps... course overview and curriculum

courses.title: Tailwind CSS 4+
courses.description: I'd been using Tailwind CSS somewhat reluctantly for a while, and wanted to better understand the beast. The course, which covers Tailwind's utility-first approach and advanced techniques, gifted me with a much more positive appreciation, and deeper understanding, of the framework.

courses.title: Design for Developers
courses.description: A very engaging course covering design fundamentals and patterns, then exploring the pathways to implement them in website builds. Largely a refresher, but worthwhile nevertheless.

courses.title: Mastering Chrome Dev Tools
courses.description: DevTools are such a part of daily life, and a prime target for the saying "familiarity breeds contempt". I learned new features, saw old ones with fresh eyes, and felt my debugging confidence grow. A great course.

courses.title: The Joy of React
courses.imageAlt: A happy particle system cartoon, as the Joy of React training icon
courses.description: I took this React course to refresh and deepen my understanding of the framework. It was super interesting and great fun.

courses.title: CSS for JavaScript Developers
courses.imageAlt: A happy particle system cartoon, as the CSS for JavaScript Developers training icon
courses.description: As a self-taught developer on CSS through practice not study, I wanted to develop a deeper understanding of the principles that underlie CSS. This course has been instrumental in filling gaps, and enhancing my skills.

courses.title: Whimsical Animations
courses.imageAlt: A happy particle system cartoon, as the Whimsical Animations training icon
courses.description: I've been making web-based animations for years, and when this course popped up I thought it would be good to shake myself up and learn some new techniques. The course has confirmed my growing love of SVGs, and greatly deepened my understanding of CSS animation.

intro: A small selection of the games, tools, and experiments I've made in my own time.

projects.title: Dyslexia alphabet learning tool
projects.thumbAlt: A board of scrambled letters for dyslexia game
description: When the application my dyslexic son's learning support teacher used was closed down, I remade it for her and her colleagues.
Free to use.

projects.title: Death's Hand
projects.thumbAlt: Game image of a hand drawn spaceship flying into enemies over a planet
description: Made during a hack week at Secureworks, with an idea that it could be an easter egg on a 404 page.

A horizontal scrolling invaders game, with hand-drawn graphics. Vanilla JavaScript, using ES6 modules. The first two waves of invaders are hand coded to spell a message (originally relevant as a 404), then afterwards we fall back to an endless random enemy pattern generator.
I revisited this to make a JS13K Games entry. I managed to keep it hand-drawn, and although I did need to cut the parallax environment layers I was able to add light-speed star effects.

projects.title: Stereo audio visualisation
projects.thumbAlt: Graphic of oscilloscope screens displaying patterns made by special music
description: The sound artist Jerobeam Fenderson creates music that can be visualised through an oscilloscope. I don't have an oscilloscope, so I wrote a JavaScript player that does the same thing.
This is not an animation.
The graphics are the visual output of specially created music, produced by combining the stereo waveforms.
Featured in Steve Gardner's Tiny Web Animation Newsletter.

projects.title: 3D Easter Egg Painter
projects.thumbAlt: Painting tool interface next to a 3D egg with the result displayed as a texture
description: I co-ran a team building challenge, to paint 3D Easter Eggs, then create a game or interface to use the resultant images.
My primary role was creating the initial paint application, using canvas for the main painting app, and live rendering the result onto an interactive 3D egg.
I also took responsibility for encouraging colleagues to contribute to the project, helping with the egg API.
